title: Alexa
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: A great man in Rabbi Tarfon’s time in Lod, as in [Chagigah 18a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.18a.10-11): he died on the day of slaughter after Shavuot, and all Israel went in to eulogize him, but Rabbi Tarfon did not let them. The author of Erekh Milin, p. 63, holds that he was the husband of Herod’s sister, whose name was Salome; she was his younger sister, married before Herod’s death, and he gave them Yavneh and Ashdod as a gift; and since through him great good was done for Israel, in that he saved the sages from death, as cited in Megillat Taanit and in Yosippon, therefore they eulogized him. Hyman considers this clever but false: it is known that Antipater, Herod’s father, was killed before Herod reigned, and it is known that Herod reigned thirty-four years and the beginning of his reign was a hundred and three years before the Temple [was destroyed], as in [Avodah Zarah 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.9a.1). Even if we say that she was left a small girl when her father died, she would have been at least about a hundred and ten years old at the time of the destruction; and this incident was already after the destruction, when Rabbi Tarfon was the head in Lod, for in Temple times Rabbi Tarfon was not yet so great. Hyman argues that we would have to grant Herod’s sister’s husband too long a life. The book Otzar Yisrael confused him with Alexa, the gentile judge who spoke with Rabbi Mana; Hyman rejects that identification.[^1]

notes.text: Chagigah first calls it Shavuot and then clarifies that it was the day of slaughter; see also [Heilprin’s Alexa notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=479&lang=en). Avodah Zarah gives 103 years for the dynasty of the House of Herod. The ages and identifications in the article belong to Hyman’s argument with Erekh Milin.
